title: Signal at Blue Hour
scene_label: Episode 01 · Meteor-watch week · Seaside radio observatory

background.alt: A seaside radio-observatory control terrace at blue hour with amber instrument light

appearance.label: Mio Amamiya
appearance.tagline: She maps distant signals precisely. The one between you is harder to name.
appearance.description: Quietly witty and meticulous, Mio begins the meteor watch carefully guarded, then lets her warmth show when the night takes an unexpected turn.
appearance.visual_identity: An adult woman with a dark-indigo shoulder-length bob, teal-gray eyes, a small gold four-point star hairpin, a navy research cardigan, an ivory mock-neck blouse, and a slim amber pendant
appearance.art_direction: Original polished 2D anime and moe visual-novel character art, with graceful adult proportions, clean expressive features, and a blue-hour teal, indigo, and amber palette

expression_variants.alt: Mio Amamiya with a composed, attentive expression
expression_variants.label: Composed
expression_variants.description: composed and attentive, with a restrained closed-mouth smile and direct, thoughtful eye contact

expression_variants.alt: Mio Amamiya smiling with open delight
expression_variants.label: Delighted
expression_variants.description: warm, open delight with bright eyes and an unguarded smile, preserving the same adult identity and outfit

expression_variants.label: Flustered
expression_variants.description: warmly flustered with a faint blush, softened gaze, and shy half-smile; bashful, never juvenile

expression_variants.alt: Mio Amamiya focused with a serious, concerned expression
expression_variants.label: Concerned
expression_variants.description: focused concern with drawn brows and a firm mouth, reading as a capable adult responding to a technical problem

statements.speaker: mio
statements.text: You made it. I was starting to suspect the meteor shower had better plans for you than I did.

statements.speaker: you
statements.text: The last train was late. I brought hot cocoa as an apology - and remembered the cinnamon.

statements.speaker: mio
statements.text: You remembered. That may be the most convincing research result I've seen all week.

options.text: Ask whether tonight counts as a second date.
Ask what the array is picking up.

statements.speaker: you
statements.text: Then... if the sky cooperates, could we call tonight a second date?

statements.speaker: mio
statements.text: Only if we agree the first was the night we stayed up until dawn calibrating the receiver.

statements.speaker: you
statements.text: What is the array actually hearing tonight?

statements.speaker: mio
statements.text: Mostly the sky arguing with itself. Ask again in an hour and I may have a better answer.

statements.speaker: mio
statements.text: Wait - the western array just went quiet. If that timing drift is real, we'll miss the entire event.

statements.speaker: you
statements.text: Tell me where you need me.

statements.speaker: mio
statements.text: Beside me. For the array - and, if you're willing, after the stars are done too.

statements.speaker: mio
statements.text: West cabinet, second shelf. Bring the spare timing card and we may still catch it.

stages.brief: An original observatory deck at blue hour, receiver dishes against a darkening sky, no people
The same observatory deck after full dark, instrument lamps on, no people

tracks.brief: Sparse synth pads over distant wind, patient and a little expectant
